text: It is the tears of the earth that keep her smiles in bloom.
note: sorrow and joy bound together; grief that nourishes

tags.when_helps: Someone in a sad stretch who needs to see that sorrow can feed later joy.

display_text: It is the tears of the earth that keep her smiles in bloom.
plain: The earth's tears are what keep her smiles blooming.
core_idea: Sorrow nourishes joy

text: If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.
note: dwelling on loss blinds you to what remains

tags.when_helps: Someone so absorbed in mourning what is gone that they are missing what is still here.

display_text: If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.
plain: If you weep over missing the sun, you will also miss seeing the stars.
core_idea: Grieving what's gone can blind you to what's here

text: Once we dreamt that we were strangers. We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling estranged from others who needs reminding that closeness can be rediscovered.

display_text: Once we dreamt that we were strangers. We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.
plain: We once dreamed we were strangers, and woke to find we were dear to each other.
core_idea: We are closer than we think

text: Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart like the evening among the silent trees.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose sadness is starting to settle and who wants company in that quiet.

display_text: Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart like the evening among the silent trees.
plain: The sorrow in my heart grows quiet and peaceful, like evening settling among still trees.
core_idea: Sorrow can settle into peace

text: Do not seat your love upon a precipice because it is high.
note: choosing love for status rather than safety

tags.when_helps: Someone drawn to love someone mainly for status or height, before they commit.

display_text: Do not seat your love upon a precipice because it is high.
plain: Do not place your love on a cliff edge just because it is high.
core_idea: Do not love something for its height

text: What you are you do not see, what you see is your shadow.

tags.when_helps: Someone confused about who they really are, judging themselves by surface appearances.

display_text: What you are you do not see, what you see is your shadow.
plain: You cannot see what you really are; what you see is only your shadow.
core_idea: Our true self is unseen by us

text: I cannot choose the best. The best chooses me.
note: letting go of the need to choose perfectly

tags.when_helps: Someone paralysed by the pressure to choose the perfect option.

display_text: I cannot choose the best. The best chooses me.
plain: I cannot pick the best; the best picks me.
core_idea: The best chooses us

text: They throw their shadows before them who carry their lantern on their back.
note: living by the past casts shadows ahead

tags.when_helps: Someone whose own way of looking keeps darkening the road ahead of them.

display_text: They throw their shadows before them who carry their lantern on their back.
plain: People who carry their lamp behind them cast their own shadows ahead of them.
core_idea: Light behind us darkens the path ahead

text: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling flat or jaded who could use wonder at simply being alive.

display_text: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
plain: Life is the constant surprise that I exist at all.
core_idea: Existing at all is a constant wonder

text: Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.
note: rest as part of good work

tags.when_helps: Someone overworked who feels guilty about resting and needs permission to stop.

display_text: Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.
plain: Rest belongs to work the way eyelids belong to eyes.
core_idea: Rest is part of work

text: Man is a born child, his power is the power of growth.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling small or behind who needs reminding that growth is their real strength.

display_text: Man is a born child, his power is the power of growth.
plain: A human being is born a child, and our power is the power to grow.
core_idea: Our power is growth

text: O Beauty, find thyself in love, not in the flattery of thy mirror.

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking worth in flattery or appearance rather than in loving and being loved.

display_text: O Beauty, find thyself in love, not in the flattery of thy mirror.
plain: Beauty, find yourself in love, not in your mirror's flattery.
core_idea: Beauty is found in love, not vanity

text: Life finds its wealth by the claims of the world, and its worth by the claims of love.
note: worth found in love, not worldly demands

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing worldly success who wonders what actually gives their life worth.

display_text: Life finds its wealth by the claims of the world, and its worth by the claims of love.
plain: Life gains its wealth from what the world asks of it, and its worth from what love asks of it.
core_idea: Love, not the world, gives life worth

text: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its past.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose past contributions are forgotten now that they have less to give.

display_text: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its past.
plain: A dried-up riverbed gets no thanks for the water it once carried.
core_idea: Past service is soon forgotten

text: The bird wishes it were a cloud. The cloud wishes it were a bird.
note: envy; wanting to be someone else

tags.when_helps: Someone wishing they were someone else, unaware others envy them too.

display_text: The bird wishes it were a cloud. The cloud wishes it were a bird.
plain: The bird wishes to be a cloud, and the cloud wishes to be a bird.
core_idea: Everyone longs to be something else

text: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."
note: freedom as the source of true expression

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling hemmed in who senses their voice will only come with freedom.

display_text: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."
plain: The waterfall sings that it finds its song when it finds its freedom.
core_idea: Freedom brings out our song

text: Do not blame your food because you have no appetite.
note: blaming circumstances for your own state

tags.when_helps: Someone blaming circumstances for a dullness that actually starts within them.

display_text: Do not blame your food because you have no appetite.
plain: Do not blame the food when you are the one without appetite.
core_idea: The fault may lie in us

text: You smiled and talked to me of nothing and I felt that for this I had been waiting long.
note: quiet companionship one has longed for

tags.when_helps: Someone savouring simple, easy closeness with a person they love.

display_text: You smiled and talked to me of nothing and I felt that for this I had been waiting long.
plain: You smiled and talked to me about nothing, and I felt this was what I had long been waiting for.
core_idea: Simple closeness is what we wait for

text: He has made his weapons his gods. When his weapons win he is defeated himself.
note: trusting force; winning that defeats you

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to win at any cost, who needs to see what force does to the winner.

display_text: He has made his weapons his gods. When his weapons win he is defeated himself.
plain: He has turned his weapons into gods; when his weapons win, he himself is defeated.
core_idea: Worshipping force defeats us

text: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid of looking small who needs courage to show up anyway.

display_text: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.
plain: The stars are not afraid of looking as small as fireflies.
core_idea: True greatness does not fear seeming small

text: The mind, sharp but not broad, sticks at every point but does not move.

tags.when_helps: Someone stuck overanalysing details who needs a broader view to move forward.

display_text: The mind, sharp but not broad, sticks at every point but does not move.
plain: A mind that is sharp but narrow catches on every detail and never moves forward.
core_idea: Sharpness without breadth gets stuck

text: Man does not reveal himself in his history, he struggles up through it.

tags.when_helps: Someone defined by their past who needs to see they are still climbing through it.

display_text: Man does not reveal himself in his history, he struggles up through it.
plain: People do not show who they are in their history; they struggle upward through it.
core_idea: We rise through history, not in it

text: Like the meeting of the seagulls and the waves we meet and come near. The seagulls fly off, the waves roll away and we depart.

tags.when_helps: Someone parting from people they met briefly, accepting that meetings pass.

display_text: Like the meeting of the seagulls and the waves we meet and come near. The seagulls fly off, the waves roll away and we depart.
plain: We meet and draw close like seagulls and waves; then the gulls fly off, the waves roll away, and we part.
core_idea: Meetings are brief, then we part

text: My day is done, and I am like a boat drawn on the beach, listening to the dance-music of the tide in the evening.
note: ageing; the close of a working life

tags.when_helps: Someone at the end of a long working life, resting and listening to what remains.

display_text: My day is done, and I am like a boat drawn on the beach, listening to the dance-music of the tide in the evening.
plain: My day is over, and I am like a boat pulled up on the beach, listening to the tide's dance music in the evening.
core_idea: Resting peacefully at the end of the day

text: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.

tags.when_helps: Someone looking for meaning who might find it in giving themselves to others.

display_text: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.
plain: Life is handed to us as a gift, but we make it truly ours by giving it away.
core_idea: We earn life by giving it

text: We come nearest to the great when we are great in humility.

tags.when_helps: Someone admiring greatness who wants to grow towards it through humility.

display_text: We come nearest to the great when we are great in humility.
plain: We get closest to greatness when our humility is great.
core_idea: Great humility brings us near greatness

text: The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.
note: burdens of status; pity for the proud

tags.when_helps: Someone envying showy success who might see the weight it carries.

display_text: The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.
plain: The little sparrow feels sorry for the peacock, which has to carry its heavy, showy tail.
core_idea: Splendour can be a burden

text: Never be afraid of the moments--thus sings the voice of the everlasting.

tags.when_helps: Someone gripped by fear of the moment ahead who needs steadying.

display_text: Never be afraid of the moments--thus sings the voice of the everlasting.
plain: The eternal voice sings to us: do not be afraid of passing moments.
core_idea: Do not fear the passing moments

text: Take my wine in my own cup, friend. It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.
note: being valued as yourself, not compared

tags.when_helps: Someone pressured to fit others' moulds who wants to stay true to themselves.

display_text: Take my wine in my own cup, friend. It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.
plain: Friend, take my wine in my own cup; poured into someone else's, it loses its crown of foam.
core_idea: Take something in its own form, not recast

text: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose quiet, steady support goes unnoticed, or someone wanting to thank such people.

display_text: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.
plain: Be grateful to the flame for its light, but also remember the lampstand, patiently and faithfully holding it up out of sight in the shadow.
core_idea: Remember the unseen supporters behind the visible

text: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling small and slow who needs to see their quiet strength.

display_text: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.
plain: Little grass, your steps are tiny, yet the whole earth beneath you is yours.
core_idea: The small still hold the earth

text: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.

tags.when_helps: Someone who lost while doing right, needing to see that losing does not undo integrity.

display_text: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.
plain: What is wrong cannot survive losing, but what is right can lose and still endure.
core_idea: Right can survive defeat; wrong cannot

text: "I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."

tags.when_helps: Someone with plenty to give who wants to give generously and gladly.

display_text: "I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."
plain: The waterfall sings that it gives all its water joyfully, even though the thirsty need only a little.
core_idea: Give everything joyfully, beyond what is needed

text: The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree. The tree gave it.
note: betrayal; giving to those who harm

tags.when_helps: Someone whose generosity has been turned against them, or who reflects on giving to those who harm.

display_text: The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree. The tree gave it.
plain: The woodcutter's axe asked the tree for a handle, and the tree gave it.
core_idea: The tree gives the means of its own cutting

text: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.
note: blaming the world for our misreading

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling betrayed by the world who might question their own reading of it.

display_text: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.
plain: We misread the world and then claim that it has fooled us.
core_idea: We misread the world, then blame it

text: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth. The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.

tags.when_helps: Someone who craves solitude while others seek company, wondering if that is all right.

display_text: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth. The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.
plain: Grass looks for company down in the earth, while the tree looks for solitude up in the sky.
core_idea: Some seek company, others seek solitude

text: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.

tags.when_helps: Someone thinking about death who wants to imagine life and its end both lived beautifully.

display_text: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.
plain: May life be as beautiful as summer flowers, and death as beautiful as autumn leaves.
core_idea: Life and death can both be beautiful

text: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.

tags.when_helps: Someone trying hard to do good who feels shut out, needing to lead with love.

display_text: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.
plain: Someone who wants to do good has to knock at the gate; someone who loves finds it already open.
core_idea: Love opens doors that good intentions knock on

text: The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.

tags.when_helps: Someone in a dull supporting role who wants to value the protection they provide.

display_text: The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.
plain: The sheath is happy to be plain and dull, because it keeps the sword sharp.
core_idea: Humble roles protect what shines

text: Power said to the world, "You are mine. The world kept it prisoner on her throne. Love said to the world, "I am thine." The world gave it the freedom of her house.

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to control others, or feeling controlled, who needs to see love gives freedom.

display_text: Power said to the world, "You are mine. The world kept it prisoner on her throne. Love said to the world, "I am thine." The world gave it the freedom of her house.
plain: Power claimed the world as its own, and the world made it a prisoner on her throne. Love gave itself to the world, and the world let it move freely in her home.
core_idea: Power is confined; love is set free

text: I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.
note: peace about being forgotten and passing

tags.safety_reason: Presents passing away and being forgotten as a felt freedom.
tags.when_helps: A reflective reader at ease contemplating how all lives pass and are forgotten; not for someone in distress.

display_text: I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.
plain: I think of past ages that drifted through life, love and death and are now forgotten, and I feel how freeing it is to pass away.
core_idea: Being forgotten by time can feel freeing

text: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.

tags.when_helps: Someone troubled by mortality who might see death as what makes life precious.

display_text: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.
plain: Death is like the stamp that gives a coin its value: because life ends, we can spend it on what really matters.
core_idea: Death gives life its value

text: The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky. The morning crowned it with splendour.

tags.when_helps: Someone staying modest and unnoticed who needs to trust that humility is honoured.

display_text: The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky. The morning crowned it with splendour.
plain: The cloud stayed modestly in a corner of the sky, and the morning crowned it with glory.
core_idea: Humility is crowned with glory

text: The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who has been insulted and is deciding how to answer.

display_text: The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.
plain: The dust is insulted, and in return it gives flowers.
core_idea: Answer insult with gifts

text: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.

tags.when_helps: Someone clinging to good moments, afraid to let them pass and move on.

display_text: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.
plain: Don't stop to pick and hoard flowers; keep walking, because flowers will go on blooming all along your way.
core_idea: Don't cling to beauty; more will come

text: Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to flatter or inflate a friend rather than see them truly.

display_text: Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.
plain: Don't insult your friend by crediting him with good qualities that are really your own.
core_idea: Don't patronise friends with borrowed virtues

text: I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.
note: your own unlit potential blocks you

tags.when_helps: Someone getting in their own way who senses an inner light not yet awakened.

display_text: I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.
plain: My own shadow falls across my path because the lamp I carry has never been lit.
core_idea: Our unlit inner light darkens our way

text: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.

tags.when_helps: Someone using noise and crowds to avoid their own inner silence.

display_text: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.
plain: People go into noisy crowds to drown out the loud silence inside themselves.
core_idea: Crowds are used to escape inner silence

text: The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.

tags.when_helps: Someone lonely in a crowd, surrounded by people yet unloved.

display_text: The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.
plain: The road is lonely even though crowds walk it, because no one loves it.
core_idea: Crowded but unloved is still lonely

text: I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.
note: carrying past failures within present success

tags.when_helps: Someone carrying past failures who might see them as part of what now flourishes.

display_text: I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.
plain: Within my thriving world I carry all the worlds that failed.
core_idea: Success carries past failures within it

text: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.

tags.when_helps: Someone pushing hard to shape themselves or another, who needs gentleness instead.

display_text: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.
plain: It is not hammer blows but the water's dancing that sings the pebbles into perfect shape.
core_idea: Gentleness perfects more than force

text: Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave. The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.

tags.when_helps: Someone taking without thanks, or noticing entitlement in themselves.

display_text: Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave. The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.
plain: Bees drink nectar from flowers and hum their thanks as they leave, while the showy butterfly is sure the flowers should thank him.
core_idea: The humble give thanks; the vain expect it

text: To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.
note: bluntness that is not full honesty

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone proud of bluntness who should ask whether they are telling the whole truth.

display_text: To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.
plain: It is easy to speak bluntly when you don't wait until you can tell the whole truth.
core_idea: Bluntness is easy without the whole truth

text: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.
note: fear of mistakes shuts out truth

tags.when_helps: Someone so afraid of mistakes that they close themselves to learning.

display_text: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.
plain: If you close your door to every mistake, you will close it to truth as well.
core_idea: Shutting out all error shuts out truth

text: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.

tags.when_helps: Someone doing hidden, unrewarded work that makes others' success possible.

display_text: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.
plain: The roots underground ask no reward for making the branches bear fruit.
core_idea: Hidden helpers seek no reward

text: Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.
note: time well used versus merely passing

tags.when_helps: Someone watching the clock who wants time to feel rich rather than merely passing.

display_text: Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.
plain: Time is the richness of change, but the clock mocks it, turning it into mere change with no richness at all.
core_idea: Clocks reduce time to empty change

text: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.

tags.when_helps: Someone tired of aimless wandering who finds love once the path leads somewhere whole.

display_text: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.
plain: When you took me only from here to there, Road, I grew tired of you; now that you lead me everywhere, I love you as if married to you.
core_idea: A road to everywhere becomes beloved

text: Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.
note: hope for guidance through the unknown

tags.when_helps: Someone facing a dark, unknown future who wants to trust in some guidance.

display_text: Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.
plain: Let me believe that one of those stars is guiding my life through the dark unknown.
core_idea: Hoping a star guides us through darkness

text: One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years. It sings to me in the night,--"I loved you."

tags.when_helps: Someone haunted at night by a love that is gone.

display_text: One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years. It sings to me in the night,--"I loved you."
plain: A sad voice lives among the ruins of the years, and at night it sings to me that it loved me.
core_idea: Past love still sings in memory

text: I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.
note: neglecting what is close to home

tags.when_helps: Someone with grand ideals who feels something missing closer to home.

display_text: I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.
plain: I have stars in the sky, but oh, how I long for the little lamp in my house that is still unlit.
core_idea: Distant splendour can't replace a near light

text: The dust of the dead words clings to thee. Wash thy soul with silence.
note: silence to heal after empty words

tags.when_helps: Someone worn out by too many words and arguments who needs silence.

display_text: The dust of the dead words clings to thee. Wash thy soul with silence.
plain: The dust of dead words clings to you. Wash your soul clean with silence.
core_idea: Silence cleanses the soul of empty words

text: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling the gaps a death has left in their life.

display_text: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.
plain: Life has gaps in it, and through them comes the sad music of death.
core_idea: Death's sorrow enters through life's gaps

text: The world has opened its heart of light in the morning. Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.
note: meeting a new day with love

tags.when_helps: Someone waking to a new morning who wants to meet the day openly.

display_text: The world has opened its heart of light in the morning. Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.
plain: In the morning the world has opened its heart of light. My heart, come out with your love to meet it.
core_idea: Meet the morning's light with love

text: God's great power is in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.

tags.when_helps: Someone who equates strength with force, or who is shaken by life's storms.

display_text: God's great power is in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.
plain: God's great power is found in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.
core_idea: God's power is in gentleness, not force

text: "Who is there to take up my duties?" asked the setting sun. "I shall do what I can, my Master," said the earthen lamp.

tags.when_helps: Someone daunted by a task too big for them who can still do what they can.

display_text: "Who is there to take up my duties?" asked the setting sun. "I shall do what I can, my Master," said the earthen lamp.
plain: The setting sun asked who would take over its work, and the little clay lamp replied that it would do what it could.
core_idea: Do what small part you can

plain_judge.issue: Drops the lamp addressing the sun as 'my Master'.

text: By plucking her petals you do not gather the beauty of the flower.

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to possess what they admire, damaging it in the process.

display_text: By plucking her petals you do not gather the beauty of the flower.
plain: Pulling off a flower's petals does not get you its beauty.
core_idea: Taking apart beauty does not capture it

text: The Great walks with the Small without fear. The Middling keeps aloof.

tags.when_helps: Someone keeping a status distance from others, or hurt by those who do.

display_text: The Great walks with the Small without fear. The Middling keeps aloof.
plain: The truly great mix with the small without fear; it is those in the middle who hold themselves apart.
core_idea: The great are not afraid of the small

text: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.
note: giving from a sense of fullness

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling full and ready to give generously from that abundance.

display_text: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.
plain: When we delight in being full, we can give away what we produce with joy.
core_idea: Fullness lets us give gladly

text: Love! when you come with the burning lamp of pain in your hand, I can see your face and know you as bliss.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose love has brought pain, seeking meaning in it.

display_text: Love! when you come with the burning lamp of pain in your hand, I can see your face and know you as bliss.
plain: Love, when you come carrying the burning lamp of pain, I can see your face and recognise you as joy.
core_idea: Pain reveals love's face as bliss

text: The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.

tags.when_helps: Someone in pain who might turn it into something creative.

display_text: The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.
plain: The world has touched my soul with pain and asks me to give it back as songs.
core_idea: Turn the world's pain into song

text: Either you have work or you have not. When you have to say, "Let us do something," then begins mischief.

tags.when_helps: Someone idle and restless, tempted to make trouble for want of real work.

display_text: Either you have work or you have not. When you have to say, "Let us do something," then begins mischief.
plain: Either you have real work or you don't. Trouble starts when you have to say, 'Let's do something.'
core_idea: Trouble begins with aimless busyness

text: "Who drives me forward like fate?" "The Myself striding on my back."

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling driven by fate who might see their own self pushing them.

display_text: "Who drives me forward like fate?" "The Myself striding on my back."
plain: Asked what drives him on like fate, the answer is: his own self, striding on his back.
core_idea: Our own self drives us like fate

text: I spill water from my water jar as I walk on my way, Very little remains for my home.
note: giving away so much little is left for home

tags.when_helps: Someone who gives so much on the way that little is left for home.

display_text: I spill water from my water jar as I walk on my way, Very little remains for my home.
plain: As I walk I keep spilling water from my jar, so very little is left by the time I get home.
core_idea: What we carry spills away on the road

text: The water in a vessel is sparkling; the water in the sea is dark. The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking answers who must accept that the deepest truths resist words.

display_text: The water in a vessel is sparkling; the water in the sea is dark. The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.
plain: Water in a jar sparkles while the sea is dark. A small truth can be said in clear words; a great truth is met with deep silence.
core_idea: Great truths are held in silence

text: It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones,-- great things are for everyone.
note: small personal gifts to loved ones

tags.when_helps: Someone thinking about what they truly leave behind for the people they love.

display_text: It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones,-- great things are for everyone.
plain: What I leave to the people I love are the little things; the great things belong to everyone.
core_idea: Little things are our gifts to loved ones

text: My flower of the day dropped its petals forgotten. In the evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose ordinary days have passed unnoticed and are now treasured as memory.

display_text: My flower of the day dropped its petals forgotten. In the evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.
plain: My flower of the day lost its petals unnoticed, but by evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.
core_idea: Lost moments ripen into precious memories

text: He who is too busy doing good finds no time to be good.
note: busy doing good versus being good

tags.when_helps: Someone so busy with good causes that they neglect being good.

display_text: He who is too busy doing good finds no time to be good.
plain: Someone too busy doing good has no time left to actually be good.
core_idea: Busy doing good, too busy to be good

text: I am the autumn cloud, empty of rain, see my fulness in the field of ripened rice.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling used up who needs to see their worth in what they have nourished.

display_text: I am the autumn cloud, empty of rain, see my fulness in the field of ripened rice.
plain: I am like the autumn cloud that has already poured out its rain; look for my fullness in the ripe rice fields.
core_idea: What we gave shows where our fullness went

text: Darkness travels towards light, but blindness towards death.
note: ignorance that seeks versus refuses to see

tags.when_helps: Someone in a dark season who needs to see the difference between darkness and blindness.

display_text: Darkness travels towards light, but blindness towards death.
plain: Darkness moves toward light, but blindness moves toward death.
core_idea: Darkness can end in light; blindness cannot

text: Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust. Let the world find its way to you.
note: stillness; letting things come to you

tags.when_helps: Someone agitated and striving who needs to sit still and let life come to them.

display_text: Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust. Let the world find its way to you.
plain: Be still, my heart, and don't stir up dust. Let the world come to you.
core_idea: Be still and let the world come

text: The bow whispers to the arrow before it speeds forth--"Your freedom is mine."
note: parenting; letting go of someone you love

tags.when_helps: A parent letting a child go who finds their own freedom in the child's flight.

display_text: The bow whispers to the arrow before it speeds forth--"Your freedom is mine."
plain: Before the arrow flies, the bow whispers to it that its freedom belongs to the bow.
core_idea: Freedom depends on what launches it

plain_judge.issue: 'Belongs to the bow' narrows 'your freedom is mine' to ownership.

text: A mind all logic is like a knife all blade. It makes the hand bleed that uses it.
note: too much logic hurts the thinker

tags.when_helps: Someone relying on logic alone who keeps hurting themselves and others.

display_text: A mind all logic is like a knife all blade. It makes the hand bleed that uses it.
plain: A mind that is nothing but logic is like a knife that is all blade: it cuts the hand of whoever uses it.
core_idea: Pure logic wounds its user

text: By touching you may kill, by keeping away you may possess.

tags.when_helps: Someone gripping what they love too tightly, at risk of crushing it.

display_text: By touching you may kill, by keeping away you may possess.
plain: Touching something can kill it, while keeping your distance may let you truly have it.
core_idea: Grasping destroys; distance can possess

text: The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the neighbouring bees is too small. His neighbours ask him to build one still smaller.
note: envy and petty criticism of others

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone criticising others' work who is invited to do better themselves.

display_text: The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the neighbouring bees is too small. His neighbours ask him to build one still smaller.
plain: The wasp thinks the bees' honeycomb next door is too small, and the bees tell him to build an even smaller one.
core_idea: Critics should try making something themselves

text: "I cannot keep your waves," says the bank to the river. "Let me keep your footprints in my heart."

tags.when_helps: Someone who cannot keep a loved one but wants to hold their memory.

display_text: "I cannot keep your waves," says the bank to the river. "Let me keep your footprints in my heart."
plain: The riverbank tells the river that it cannot hold on to its waves, but asks to keep its footprints in its heart.
core_idea: We can't keep what passes, only its traces

text: Let me not put myself wrongly to my world and set it against me.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone who feels the world is against them and wonders if their own stance causes it.

display_text: Let me not put myself wrongly to my world and set it against me.
plain: May I not present myself wrongly to the world and so turn it against me.
core_idea: Don't turn the world against yourself

text: Praise shames me, for I secretly beg for it.

tags.when_helps: Someone uneasy at praise because they know how much they want it.

display_text: Praise shames me, for I secretly beg for it.
plain: Praise makes me ashamed, because secretly I beg for it.
core_idea: Craving praise makes praise shameful

text: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing to do become untroubled in its depth of peace like the evening in the seashore when the water is silent.

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels guilty or uneasy when they have nothing to do.

display_text: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing to do become untroubled in its depth of peace like the evening in the seashore when the water is silent.
plain: When I have nothing to do, may my idleness be deeply peaceful and untroubled, like evening on the shore when the water is still.
core_idea: Let idle time be deeply peaceful

text: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow to the mere mists and vapours of life.
note: desire colouring how we see life

tags.when_helps: Someone noticing how wanting colours and inflates what they chase.

display_text: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow to the mere mists and vapours of life.
plain: Our desires paint rainbow colours onto what are only mists and vapours in life.
core_idea: Desire colours life's empty mists

text: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their own names.

tags.when_helps: Someone with sad thoughts they cannot quite name.

display_text: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their own names.
plain: My sad thoughts tease me by asking me what they are called.
core_idea: Sadness asks to be named

text: The service of the fruit is precious, the service of the flower is sweet, but let my service be the service of the leaves in its shade of humble devotion.

tags.when_helps: Someone content to serve quietly in the background, seeking meaning in humble work.

display_text: The service of the fruit is precious, the service of the flower is sweet, but let my service be the service of the leaves in its shade of humble devotion.
plain: The fruit's service is precious and the flower's is sweet, but may my service be like the leaves, giving shade in humble devotion.
core_idea: Choose humble, devoted service like leaves

text: Men are cruel, but Man is kind.

tags.when_helps: Someone hurt by cruel people who needs to keep faith in humanity.

display_text: Men are cruel, but Man is kind.
plain: People as individuals can be cruel, but humanity as a whole is kind.
core_idea: Men are cruel, humanity is kind

text: The world does not leak because death is not a crack.
note: death does not diminish the world

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels death has broken the world and needs to see it still holds.

display_text: The world does not leak because death is not a crack.
plain: Nothing drains out of the world when someone dies, because death is not a crack in it.
core_idea: Death is not a hole in the world

text: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.

tags.when_helps: Someone mourning a lost love who might see how it enriched their life.

display_text: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.
plain: Love that has been lost has made life richer.
core_idea: Lost love enriches life

text: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from the earth.
note: anger and force bring no good

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to lash out who needs to see force yields nothing.

display_text: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from the earth.
plain: Kicking the ground only raises dust; it never grows crops.
core_idea: Anger and force produce nothing

text: Our names are the light that glows on the sea waves at night and then dies without leaving its signature.

tags.when_helps: Someone anxious about legacy and fame, facing how names fade.

display_text: Our names are the light that glows on the sea waves at night and then dies without leaving its signature.
plain: Our names are like light glowing on night waves at sea, which fades without leaving a trace.
core_idea: Our names fade without a trace

text: Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.

tags.when_helps: Someone fixed on flaws, or criticising, who needs to see the good first.

display_text: Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.
plain: Only someone who can see the rose should be allowed to see the thorns.
core_idea: Only see faults if you see beauty too

text: Set bird's wings with gold and it will never again soar in the sky.

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted by wealth or comfort that could cost them their freedom.

display_text: Set bird's wings with gold and it will never again soar in the sky.
plain: Cover a bird's wings in gold and it will never fly in the sky again.
core_idea: Riches can ground the free spirit

text: In heart's perspective the distance looms large.
note: distance felt more in the heart

tags.when_helps: Someone separated from a loved one, feeling the distance keenly.

display_text: In heart's perspective the distance looms large.
plain: To the heart, distance seems much larger than it is.
core_idea: The heart magnifies distance

plain_judge.issue: Adds 'than it is', a slight claim beyond 'looms large'.

text: The moon has her light all over the sky, her dark spots to herself.

tags.when_helps: Someone keeping their private darkness to themselves while still giving light.

display_text: The moon has her light all over the sky, her dark spots to herself.
plain: The moon spreads her light across the whole sky and keeps her dark spots to herself.
core_idea: Share your light, keep your flaws private

text: Do not say, "It is morning," and dismiss it with a name of yesterday. See it for the first time as a new-born child that has no name.

tags.when_helps: Someone jaded by routine who wants to see the day freshly.

display_text: Do not say, "It is morning," and dismiss it with a name of yesterday. See it for the first time as a new-born child that has no name.
plain: Don't just say 'It's morning' and brush it off with yesterday's label. See it for the first time, like a newborn child without a name.
core_idea: See each morning as completely new

text: The raindrop whispered to the jasmine, "Keep me in your heart for ever." The jasmine sighed, "Alas," and dropped to the ground.

tags.when_helps: Someone wishing to be remembered forever, facing that all things fall.

display_text: The raindrop whispered to the jasmine, "Keep me in your heart for ever." The jasmine sighed, "Alas," and dropped to the ground.
plain: The raindrop asked the jasmine to keep it in her heart forever; the jasmine sighed 'Alas' and fell to the ground.
core_idea: Nothing can promise to keep us forever

text: Timid thoughts, do not be afraid of me. I am a poet.

tags.when_helps: Someone with shy, fragile thoughts who needs to treat them gently.

display_text: Timid thoughts, do not be afraid of me. I am a poet.
plain: Shy thoughts, don't be afraid of me; I am a poet.
core_idea: A poet welcomes timid thoughts

text: Thou hast led me through my crowded travels of the day to my evening's loneliness. I wait for its meaning through the stillness of the night.
note: loneliness at day's end; seeking meaning

tags.when_helps: Someone alone after a busy day, waiting quietly for meaning to come.

display_text: Thou hast led me through my crowded travels of the day to my evening's loneliness. I wait for its meaning through the stillness of the night.
plain: You have led me through the busy journeys of the day to the loneliness of evening, and I wait through the quiet night to learn what it means.
core_idea: Waiting in stillness for life's meaning

text: This life is the crossing of a sea, where we meet in the same narrow ship. In death we reach the shore and go to our different worlds.
note: companionship in life, parting in death

tags.when_helps: Someone parted by death who reflects on the shared journey before the shore.

display_text: This life is the crossing of a sea, where we meet in the same narrow ship. In death we reach the shore and go to our different worlds.
plain: Life is like crossing a sea together in one small boat; at death we reach the shore and each go off to our own world.
core_idea: We share life's voyage, part at death

text: The stream of truth flows through its channels of mistakes.

tags.when_helps: Someone ashamed of mistakes who needs to see truth emerges through them.

display_text: The stream of truth flows through its channels of mistakes.
plain: Truth flows like a stream, and the channels it runs through are our mistakes.
core_idea: Truth reaches us through mistakes

text: My heart is homesick to-day for the one sweet hour across the sea of time.
note: nostalgia, homesick for a past moment

tags.when_helps: Someone homesick for a sweet moment in the past.

display_text: My heart is homesick to-day for the one sweet hour across the sea of time.
plain: Today my heart longs, like someone homesick, for one sweet hour far back across the sea of time.
core_idea: Longing for one sweet hour long past

text: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for being blunt.

tags.when_helps: Someone in a sharp role tempted to mock those who quietly support them.

display_text: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for being blunt.
plain: The sharp blade should not sneer at its handle for being blunt.
core_idea: Don't scorn the plain parts that support you

text: The real with its meaning read wrong and emphasis misplaced is the unreal.

tags.when_helps: Someone whose picture of reality has been distorted by misreading what matters.

display_text: The real with its meaning read wrong and emphasis misplaced is the unreal.
plain: When what is real is misunderstood and the stress is put in the wrong place, it becomes unreal.
core_idea: Misread reality becomes unreal

text: Find your beauty, my heart, from the world's movement, like the boat that has the grace of the wind and the water.

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking their beauty who might find it by moving with life.

display_text: Find your beauty, my heart, from the world's movement, like the boat that has the grace of the wind and the water.
plain: My heart, find your beauty in the movement of the world, as a boat takes its grace from the wind and the water.
core_idea: Find beauty by moving with the world

text: I live in this little world of mine and am afraid to make it the least less. Lift me into thy world and let me have the freedom gladly to lose my all.
note: fear of loss; freedom of letting go

tags.when_helps: Someone clinging to a small, safe life who longs for the courage to let go.

display_text: I live in this little world of mine and am afraid to make it the least less. Lift me into thy world and let me have the freedom gladly to lose my all.
plain: I live in my own little world and fear losing even the smallest part of it. Lift me into your world, and let me be free to gladly lose everything.
core_idea: Freedom in gladly losing everything to God

text: The false can never grow into truth by growing in power.
note: power does not make falsehood true

tags.when_helps: Someone watching falsehood gain power who needs to trust it cannot become truth.

display_text: The false can never grow into truth by growing in power.
plain: Something false can never become true just by becoming more powerful.
core_idea: Power cannot make falsehood true

text: The little flower lies in the dust. It sought the path of the butterfly.

situations: loss of a dream or plan
tags.when_helps: Someone who reached beyond their nature and fell, reflecting on what went wrong.

display_text: The little flower lies in the dust. It sought the path of the butterfly.
plain: The little flower lies in the dust because it tried to follow the butterfly's path.
core_idea: Trying to be what you're not brings a fall

text: I have sung the songs of thy day. In the evening let me carry thy lamp through the stormy path.

tags.when_helps: Someone facing a hard later stretch of life who wants to carry faith into it.

display_text: I have sung the songs of thy day. In the evening let me carry thy lamp through the stormy path.
plain: I have sung the songs of your day; in the evening, let me carry your lamp along the stormy path.
core_idea: Serving God through day and stormy night

text: I do not ask thee into the house. Come into my infinite loneliness, my Lover.

tags.when_helps: Someone in deep loneliness who seeks the divine as a companion.

display_text: I do not ask thee into the house. Come into my infinite loneliness, my Lover.
plain: I don't invite you into my house; I ask you, my Lover, to come into my endless loneliness.
core_idea: Inviting the beloved into one's loneliness

text: Death belongs to life as birth does. The walk is in the raising of the foot as in the laying of it down.

tags.when_helps: Someone frightened by death who needs to see it as a natural part of life.

display_text: Death belongs to life as birth does. The walk is in the raising of the foot as in the laying of it down.
plain: Death is as much a part of life as birth, just as walking is lifting your foot as well as putting it down.
core_idea: Death belongs to life like birth

text: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy whispers in flowers and sunshine--teach me to know thy words in pain and death.
note: seeking meaning in pain and death

tags.when_helps: Someone whose faith came easily in good times, now seeking it in pain.

display_text: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy whispers in flowers and sunshine--teach me to know thy words in pain and death.
plain: I have understood what you whisper through flowers and sunshine; now teach me to understand what you say through pain and death.
core_idea: Learning God's meaning in pain and death

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'simple' from 'the simple meaning of thy whispers'.

text: Through the sadness of all things I hear the crooning of the Eternal Mother.

tags.when_helps: Someone in deep sadness who wants to feel a tender presence beneath it.

display_text: Through the sadness of all things I hear the crooning of the Eternal Mother.
plain: Beneath the sadness of everything, I hear the Eternal Mother softly singing.
core_idea: The Eternal Mother sings through all sadness

text: I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.
note: a life well lived; leaving as a friend

tags.when_helps: Someone near the end of a stay, or of life, grateful for how the place became home.

display_text: I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.
plain: My earth, I arrived on your shore a stranger, lived in your home as a guest, and leave your door as a friend.
core_idea: Arriving a stranger, leaving the earth a friend

text: Let my thoughts come to you, when I am gone, like the afterglow of sunset at the margin of starry silence.

tags.when_helps: Someone thinking about how they want to be remembered after they die.

display_text: Let my thoughts come to you, when I am gone, like the afterglow of sunset at the margin of starry silence.
plain: When I am gone, may my thoughts reach you like the lingering glow after sunset at the edge of the silent, starry night.
core_idea: Being remembered like a sunset's afterglow

text: The day of work is done. Hide my face in your arms, Mother. Let me dream.
note: rest after work; need for comfort

tags.when_helps: Someone worn out at the end of a hard day who longs to be held and rest.

display_text: The day of work is done. Hide my face in your arms, Mother. Let me dream.
plain: The day's work is over. Mother, let me hide my face in your arms and dream.
core_idea: Resting in the Mother's arms after work

text: The lamp of meeting burns long; it goes out in a moment at the parting.
note: parting and how fast it comes

tags.when_helps: Someone stunned by how suddenly a long bond ended.

display_text: The lamp of meeting burns long; it goes out in a moment at the parting.
plain: The lamp of being together burns a long time, but at parting it goes out in an instant.
core_idea: Togetherness lasts long, parting is instant

text: One word keep for me in thy silence, O World, when I am dead, "I have loved."
note: wanting to be remembered as loving

tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on what matters at the end: that they loved.

display_text: One word keep for me in thy silence, O World, when I am dead, "I have loved."
plain: World, when I am dead, keep just one phrase for me in your silence: 'I have loved.'
core_idea: Be remembered only for having loved

text: We live in this world when we love it.

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling disconnected from life who might return through loving it.

display_text: We live in this world when we love it.
plain: We truly live in this world only when we love it.
core_idea: Loving the world is truly living

text: Let the dead have the immortality of fame, but the living the immortality of love.

tags.when_helps: Someone worried about legacy who might value love over fame.

display_text: Let the dead have the immortality of fame, but the living the immortality of love.
plain: Let the dead live on through fame, but let the living live on through love.
core_idea: Fame for the dead, love for the living

text: I shall die again and again to know that life is inexhaustible.

tags.when_helps: For someone frightened by death or endings who could use a sense that life keeps renewing itself.

display_text: I shall die again and again to know that life is inexhaustible.
plain: I will die over and over to learn that life never runs out.
core_idea: Repeated deaths show life is endless

text: While I was passing with the crowd in the road I saw thy smile from the balcony and I sang and forgot all noise.
note: love lifting one above the crowd

tags.when_helps: For someone newly in love, when one glimpse of a person makes the noisy world fall away.

display_text: While I was passing with the crowd in the road I saw thy smile from the balcony and I sang and forgot all noise.
plain: Walking in the crowded road, I saw your smile from the balcony, and I sang and forgot all the noise.
core_idea: One smile can silence the world's noise

text: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.

tags.when_helps: For someone feeling the fullness of love who wants words for how it makes life complete.

display_text: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.
plain: Love is life at its fullest, like a cup filled with wine.
core_idea: Love is life filled to the brim

text: Love's pain sang round my life like the unplumbed sea, and love's joy sang like birds in its flowering groves.
note: the pain and joy of love

tags.when_helps: For someone feeling both the pain and the joy of loving, needing to see that both belong to it.

display_text: Love's pain sang round my life like the unplumbed sea, and love's joy sang like birds in its flowering groves.
plain: The pain of love surrounded my life like a bottomless sea, and the joy of love sang like birds in its blossoming woods.
core_idea: Love brings both deep pain and joy

text: Put out the lamp when thou wishest. I shall know thy darkness and shall love it.

tags.when_helps: For a believer facing a dark season who wants to trust and love God even there.

display_text: Put out the lamp when thou wishest. I shall know thy darkness and shall love it.
plain: Put out the lamp whenever you wish; I will come to know your darkness and love it.
core_idea: Loving God's darkness as well as light

text: When I stand before thee at the day's end thou shalt see my scars and know that I had my wounds and also my healing.

tags.when_helps: For someone carrying old wounds who needs to know their scars also show their healing.

display_text: When I stand before thee at the day's end thou shalt see my scars and know that I had my wounds and also my healing.
plain: When I stand before you at the end of the day, you will see my scars and know I was wounded and also healed.
core_idea: Scars show both wounds and healing

text: Clouds come floating into my life from other days no longer to shed rain or usher storm but to give colour to my sunset sky.

tags.when_helps: For someone late in life looking back on past storms, ready to see them as colour rather than pain.

display_text: Clouds come floating into my life from other days no longer to shed rain or usher storm but to give colour to my sunset sky.
plain: Clouds from past days drift into my life, no longer bringing rain or storms, only colour for my sunset sky.
core_idea: Old troubles become colour in later life

text: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters its seeds broadcast.

tags.when_helps: For someone facing backlash for speaking the truth, who needs to see opposition can spread it.

display_text: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters its seeds broadcast.
plain: Truth stirs up a storm against itself, and that storm spreads its seeds far and wide.
core_idea: Opposition spreads the truth

text: The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.

tags.when_helps: For someone just through a hard night or crisis, beginning to notice calm returning.

display_text: The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.
plain: Last night's storm has left this morning crowned with a golden calm.
core_idea: Peace follows the storm

text: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine his truth.

tags.when_helps: For someone gaining recognition who wants to stay true rather than live up to an image.

display_text: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine his truth.
plain: Blessed is the person whose fame does not shine brighter than their truth.
core_idea: Let your truth outshine your fame

text: The world loved man when he smiled. The world became afraid of him when he laughed.

tags.when_helps: For someone puzzled by how others react to their full self, wondering why openness can unsettle people.

display_text: The world loved man when he smiled. The world became afraid of him when he laughed.
plain: The world loved people when they smiled, and grew afraid of them when they laughed.
core_idea: Smiles are loved, laughter can be feared

text: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.

tags.when_helps: For someone in a low, wintry season who needs to feel trusted that spring will return.

display_text: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.
plain: Your sunshine smiles on the winter days of my heart, never doubting that spring flowers will come.
core_idea: God's light trusts the heart's coming spring

text: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to reach the moment of fulfilment.

tags.when_helps: For someone after long barren years who needs hope that fulfilment can still arrive.

display_text: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to reach the moment of fulfilment.
plain: You cross deserts of empty years to reach the moment when everything is fulfilled.
core_idea: Barren years lead to fulfilment

text: Cheerless is the day, the light under frowning clouds is like a punished child with traces of tears on its pale cheeks, and the cry of the wind is like the cry of a wounded world. But I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.
note: gloomy day, hope of meeting a friend

tags.when_helps: For someone on a grey, sorrowful day who needs a sense they are still heading toward something good.

display_text: Cheerless is the day, the light under frowning clouds is like a punished child with traces of tears on its pale cheeks, and the cry of the wind is like the cry of a wounded world. But I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.
plain: The day is gloomy: the light under the dark clouds looks like a punished, tear-stained child, and the wind cries like a wounded world. Yet I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.
core_idea: Through gloom, journeying toward the divine Friend

text: That love can ever lose is a fact that we cannot accept as truth.
note: refusing to believe love can be lost

tags.when_helps: For someone fearing or facing the loss of love, who cannot accept that love simply ends.

display_text: That love can ever lose is a fact that we cannot accept as truth.
plain: We cannot accept as true the fact that love can ever lose.
core_idea: We refuse to believe love can lose

text: We shall know some day that death can never rob us of that which our soul has gained, for her gains are one with herself.
note: death cannot take what the soul has gained

tags.when_helps: For someone grieving or facing death who needs to believe what the soul has gained is never lost.

display_text: We shall know some day that death can never rob us of that which our soul has gained, for her gains are one with herself.
plain: One day we will know that death can never take what the soul has gained, because those gains have become part of the soul itself.
core_idea: Death cannot take the soul's gains

text: God comes to me in the dusk of my evening with the flowers from my past kept fresh in his basket.
note: past joys kept fresh in later life

tags.when_helps: For someone in later life missing the past, comforted that God keeps its good things fresh.

display_text: God comes to me in the dusk of my evening with the flowers from my past kept fresh in his basket.
plain: In the evening of my life, God comes to me carrying the flowers of my past, still fresh in his basket.
core_idea: God keeps our past fresh for us

text: Let me live truly, my Lord, so that death to me become true.

tags.when_helps: For a believer thinking about death who wants to live honestly now so their end feels true.

display_text: Let me live truly, my Lord, so that death to me become true.
plain: My Lord, let me live truthfully, so that my death will be true as well.
core_idea: Live truly so death is true

text: Man's history is waiting in patience for the triumph of the insulted man.
note: patience for justice for the wronged

tags.when_helps: For someone humiliated or treated unjustly who needs to feel history is on the side of the wronged.

display_text: Man's history is waiting in patience for the triumph of the insulted man.
plain: Human history waits patiently for the day the insulted and humiliated triumph.
core_idea: History awaits the triumph of the humiliated

text: I have scaled the peak and found no shelter in fame's bleak and barren height. Lead me, my Guide, before the light fades, into the valley of quiet where life's harvest mellows into golden wisdom.
note: emptiness of fame; seeking quiet wisdom

tags.when_helps: For someone who reached success and found it empty, longing for a quieter, wiser life.

display_text: I have scaled the peak and found no shelter in fame's bleak and barren height. Lead me, my Guide, before the light fades, into the valley of quiet where life's harvest mellows into golden wisdom.
plain: I climbed to the summit and found no shelter on fame's cold, empty heights. Guide me, before the light goes, down to the quiet valley where life's harvest ripens into wisdom.
core_idea: Fame's heights are empty; wisdom grows in quiet

text: I have suffered and despaired and known death and I am glad that I am in this great world.

tags.when_helps: For someone who has been through deep suffering and wants permission to still feel glad to be alive.

display_text: I have suffered and despaired and known death and I am glad that I am in this great world.
plain: I have suffered, despaired and known death, and I am glad to be in this great world.
core_idea: Glad for life despite suffering

text: There are tracts in my life that are bare and silent. They are the open spaces where my busy days had their light and air.

tags.when_helps: For someone facing empty, quiet stretches of life who needs to see them as breathing space, not loss.

display_text: There are tracts in my life that are bare and silent. They are the open spaces where my busy days had their light and air.
plain: Some stretches of my life are bare and silent; they are the open spaces that gave my busy days light and air.
core_idea: Empty times give busy life room to breathe

text: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to me from behind making death difficult.
note: letting go of an unfulfilled past

tags.when_helps: For someone weighed down by unfinished business from the past, wishing to let it go before the end.

display_text: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to me from behind making death difficult.
plain: Free me from the unfinished past that clings to me from behind and makes dying hard.
core_idea: An unfulfilled past makes death hard

text: Let this be my last word, that I trust in thy love.

tags.when_helps: For a believer wanting to rest everything on trust in God's love.

display_text: Let this be my last word, that I trust in thy love.
plain: May my final word be this: that I trust in your love.
core_idea: Ending with trust in God's love
